correctness.rationale: The boundary Ricker two-cycle is uniquely parameterized by u=r−t,v=r+t, r=t coth(t/2)>2. At y=0 the Jacobian is upper triangular, hence λ_x=(1−u)(1−v), λ_y=q(u)q(v), q(x)=s+βx/(1+γx). Since log q is strictly concave and r=(u+v)/2, q(u)q(v)<q(r)². At coexistence onset β_eq=(1−s)(1+γr)/r, q(r)=1, so the strictly monotone transverse λ_y remains <1 and gives β_eq<β_cyc; fixed-point equation is strictly monotone in x. Near r=2+, λ_x=1−(2/3)t²+O(t⁴) so local attracting positive-state basin exists. Taylor expansion of the explicit Jensen defect gives gap 3(1−s)(4γ+1−s)(r−2)/(8(1+2γ)) plus O((r−2)²). The exact logarithmic example has q(r)=71/70, λ_y=195/196, λ_x=(1−2ln2)(1−4ln2)∈(0,1). Independently recalculated β thresholds at multiple s,γ,t and coefficient convergence. No assertion of globally attracting boundary or stable interior equilibrium.
